`touch`: make empty files.

## Synopsis

<strong>touch</strong> <em>file</em>...

## Description

<strong>touch</strong> makes each <em>file</em> that doesn't exist yet, empty. A file that exists already is left as it is. A file that can't be made is reported on standard error as <strong>touch:</strong> <em>reason</em> and the rest are still tried.

## Exit status

0 if every file exists afterwards, 1 if any could not be made.

## Notes

Unlike GNU touch, it never changes the times of a file that exists (there is no call to set them), and it has no options (<strong>-a</strong>, <strong>-m</strong>, <strong>-c</strong>, <strong>-d</strong>).

## See also

<strong>ls</strong>(1), <strong>mkdir</strong>(1), <strong>rm</strong>(1)
